 Show cause order issued vs VP Sara spokesperson over attacks on senator-judges
 by 
 Jose Cielito Reganit
 Nov 20, 2026
 11:27 AM GMT+8
 SHOW CAUSE ORDER. Senate impeachment court Presiding Officer Senator Francis “Chiz” Escudero issues a show cause order against Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesperson, lawyer Paolo Panelo, during the resumption of the hearing on Friday (Nov. 20, 2026). The order directs Panelo to explain his repeated criticisms of senator-judges, including accusations that some were biased and acting like prosecutors during the trial. (Screenshot from Senate livestream)
 MANILA – The Senate impeachment court on Friday issued a show cause order against Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesperson, lawyer Paolo Panelo, over his repeated criticisms of senator-judges, including accusations that some were biased and acting like prosecutors during the trial.
 Presiding Officer Senator Francis “Chiz” Escudero approved Senator-Judge Erwin Tulfo’s motion without objection and directed Panelo to explain his remarks on Thursday, which questioned the impartiality of several members of the impeachment court.
 Panelo accused Senators Risa Hontiveros, Francis Pangilinan, and Raffy Tulfo of showing bias in their questioning of defense witness Rainer Dela Fuente, a former Anti-Money Laundering Council official.
 He argued that challenging a witness’s credibility was the prosecution’s responsibility and urged Escudero to remind senator-judges to exercise restraint and remain impartial.
 The latest remarks followed Panelo’s public criticisms of the prosecution, which he accused on Thursday of trying to condition public opinion against Duterte.
 Tulfo raised the issue at the start of Friday’s proceedings, questioning why the vice president’s spokesperson was publicly attacking the credibility of senator-judges while Duterte is standing trial.
 “Can we do something about this, Mr. Presiding Officer? Because, I mean, he’s not party to this case. Pero siya po ang tagapagsalita ng bise presidente (But he is the spokesperson of the vice president),” he said.
 “I mean, you are the spokesperson of the vice president now on trial here, and then magkokomento ka against sa mga (you make comments against the) senator-judges, the impeachment court.”
 Tulfo said Panelo’s statements appeared disrespectful to the tribunal.
 “Eh para namang wala pong respeto sa (it appears there is a lack of respect for the) impeachment court, Mr. Presiding Officer,” he said.
 Escudero explained that Rule 18, the impeachment court’s sub judice rule, does not directly cover Panelo because he is neither a lawyer of record, a witness, nor a party to the proceedings.
 However, he said, Panelo could still be held accountable under Rule 71 of the Rules of Court, which governs contempt proceedings and applies suppletorily to the impeachment trial.
 “However, given the suppletory application of the Rules of Court, particularly Rule 71 on contempt, he may be covered or under the authority of this court,” Escudero said.
 Tulfo then formally moved to require Panelo to explain his remarks.
 “And I therefore file a motion to issue a show cause order for the spokesperson of the vice president,” he said.
 Escudero immediately approved the motion.
 “Upon motion, there being no objection, the motion is hereby approved,” Escudero ruled, directing the clerk of court to issue the show cause order.
 The order gives Panelo an opportunity to explain his remarks and does not constitute a finding of contempt.
 Panelo’s criticisms also contrasted with defense panel spokesperson Michael Poa’s position, who said Thursday that senator-judges have the right to ask questions and express their views.
 The controversy erupted as the defense continued presenting evidence against allegations of at least PHP817.87 million in unexplained wealth attributed to Duterte under Article II of the impeachment complaint. (PNA)
